subject: maths
title: Area of rectangles, triangles and parallelograms

scenes.heading: Area of rectangles, triangles and parallelograms
scenes.say: How much carpet do you need to cover your bedroom floor? That's an area question. Let's learn the formulas for rectangles, triangles and parallelograms.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Count how many 1 m square tiles cover a floor
scenes.science: Area = the number of unit squares that fit inside, e.g. 12 m²
scenes.breaks: Real tiles come whole, but area can be a decimal like 7.5 m².
scenes.say: Imagine tiling a floor with square tiles, each one metre by one metre. The area is how many tiles cover it, with no gaps. A floor four metres by three metres takes twelve tiles, so its area is twelve square metres.
scenes.caption: Imagine tiling a floor with 1 m by 1 m tiles. The area is how many tiles cover it. A floor 4 m by 3 m takes 12 tiles, so its area is 12 m².

scenes.heading: The three formulas
points: Answers in square units: cm², m²
scenes.say: Here are the formulas. A rectangle is length times width. A triangle is half of base times height, because it's half a rectangle. A parallelogram is base times height. Always give area in square units, like square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Rectangle: length × width. Triangle: ½ × base × height, because it's half a rectangle. Parallelogram: base × height. Area is in square units, like cm².

scenes.heading: Which length is the height?
scenes.say: Be careful which length you use. The height must meet the base at a right angle, like someone standing up straight. The sloping side is longer, and it doesn't go into the area formula.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. Find its area.
scenes.say: A triangle has a base of ten centimetres and a height of six centimetres. Base times height is sixty. Half of sixty is thirty. So the area is thirty square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Base 10 cm, height 6 cm. 10 × 6 = 60. Half of 60 is 30. Area = 30 cm².

scenes.heading: Parallelogram
scenes.question: A parallelogram has base 9 cm, perpendicular height 5 cm and sloping side 6 cm. Find its area.
lines: Height is 5 cm, not the 6 cm slant
scenes.say: A parallelogram has a base of nine centimetres, a height of five, and a sloping side of six. Use the height, not the slant. Nine times five is forty-five square centimetres.
scenes.caption: Base 9 cm, height 5 cm, slant 6 cm. Use the height, not the slant. 9 × 5 = 45 cm².

points: Area = space inside, in square units
scenes.say: Quick recap. Area is the space inside, in square units. Rectangle, length times width. Triangle, half base times height. Parallelogram, base times height. And the height always meets the base at a right angle. Now try the practice questions!
